novel_features.name: Traction by storefront
novel_features.description: See per-country demand signals for any app, rolled up daily, monthly, annually or all-time: new ratings, chart rank and review volume, clearly labelled as proxies.
novel_features.rationale: Apple publishes no download numbers; only a local history of per-storefront rating counts, chart ranks and reviews can turn today's values into a time series.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when asked for downloads, installs or demand by country over time; it returns honest proxies instead of invented download counts.

novel_features.name: Release and change impact
novel_features.description: Compare rank, new ratings, review stars and keyword positions in equal windows before and after a release, listing change or date.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining stored version dates and listing changes with stored chart, rating, review and keyword captures; no store endpoint returns before/after views.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to check whether a release or metadata change moved anything, with co-movement numbers and no causal claims.

novel_features.name: Cross-app change feed
novel_features.description: One dated feed of every change across your tracked apps: new versions, title and subtitle edits, price and in-app purchase price changes, privacy labels, events and featuring.
novel_features.rationale: Built from diffs between consecutive stored snapshots across apps; the store only shows each app as it is now.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for a weekly competitor review instead of opening every listing.

novel_features.name: Keyword share of voice
novel_features.description: See which apps hold the top search results across a set of tracked terms and how that share moved since the last capture.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates stored top-N result lists across many terms and captures; a live search answers one term at one moment.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it for keyword reports across a basket of terms rather than one term at a time.

novel_features.name: Multi-storefront breakouts
novel_features.description: Find apps climbing or entering the same chart in several countries at once.
novel_features.rationale: Joins stored chart snapshots across storefronts; each chart page covers one country.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to separate a multi-market breakout from noise in one storefront.

narrative.headline: Apple App Store charts, listings, ratings and reviews for any storefront from one Go binary, with a local history that turns repeated captures into rank, listing-change and traction trends.
narrative.value_prop: Pull 200-rank free and paid charts (top-grossing: up to 100 rows from Apple's legacy feed), listings with privacy labels, version history, in-app purchase prices (the page's top 10) and in-app events, and both review feeds, for any app in any storefront, with no key and no account. Every capture lands in SQLite, so traction, impact, changes, keyword-share and breakouts answer week-over-week questions once you have captures from more than one day.
narrative.auth_narrative:
No API key or Apple account. By default commands read Apple's public iTunes Lookup, Search and RSS feeds and public App Store web pages. suggest calls Apple's undocumented search-hints endpoint, and --source web (search-store, keyword-rank) and --source api (reviews) reach robots-disallowed surfaces: use those only when asked. Data is per storefront: pass --country with a two-letter code; ratings, reviews, iap, prices and compare, and the local readers traction, impact, changes, breakouts and review-digest, also take --countries for a list. Other commands read one storefront per run.

Run `app-store-pp-cli doctor` to verify setup (one paced iTunes Lookup).

Pacing: apps.apple.com pages go about 20 s apart across runs, other surfaces about 1 request per second (Search about 20 per minute). The first 403/429 stops the run (exit 7) and holds that host for at least 5 minutes, across runs; never retry in a loop.

quickstart.comment: Check configuration, resolved paths and reachability (one paced iTunes Lookup).
Fetch one full listing (Spotify) and record a snapshot.
Read a games chart and store it for movers and rank history.
Archive the newest reviews from two storefronts.
Read per-country demand proxies once some history exists.

troubleshoots.symptom: Exit code 7 or 'rate limited' after a burst of requests
troubleshoots.fix: Wait a few minutes, then retry with a narrower --countries list or a lower --rate-limit; the client stops at the first 403 or 429 on purpose and holds that host for at least 5 minutes, across runs. A 'may go only in Ns' message is the CLI's own pacing (apps.apple.com pages go about 20 s apart): nothing was sent, so rerun after that wait or raise --timeout.

troubleshoots.symptom: reviews returns no rows for an app that has reviews
troubleshoots.fix: Apple's review feed arrives in lagged batches and is sometimes empty; retry later, and keep the default --sort both (or drop an explicit --sort recent) so the helpful feed is included.

troubleshoots.symptom: impact reports insufficient_data, or traction returns empty results or null newRatings
troubleshoots.fix: These read only your local captures. Run the capture commands on more than one day: ratings, top and reviews for traction; app, ratings, top, reviews and keyword-rank for impact; app, iap, privacy, events and featured for changes; keyword-rank for keyword-share; top in several storefronts for breakouts. Schedule them daily with cron or launchd.

troubleshoots.symptom: You need real download or sales numbers
troubleshoots.fix: Apple publishes none for public apps; for apps you own, use the asc CLI (App Store Connect).

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for public App Store data on any app: listings, top charts (200 free and paid ranks), reviews across storefronts, privacy labels, version history, in-app purchase prices and in-app events. Its local SQLite history answers week-over-week questions: rank movement, listing changes, keyword share and per-country traction proxies. It needs no Apple account.
anti_triggers: Do not use it for real download, sales or revenue numbers: Apple publishes none publicly. For download questions run traction and say its numbers are proxies, never downloads; for apps you own, the asc CLI reads App Store Connect sales.
Do not use it for App Store Connect work such as builds, TestFlight, submissions or replying to reviews.
Do not use it for Apple Search Ads campaigns or keyword popularity; use apple-search-ads.
Do not use it for Google Play apps; use google-play.
Do not use it to install, buy or download apps.
